body.statement: If \(f\), \(\theta'\), and \(\kappa\) are constant on \(J\), then \(T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|\{f\theta'^2/(4\kappa)\}^{1/3}\); once this deterministic horizon lies in \([T_0,\infty)\), Theorems 1--3 reduce to a stationary canonical LR maximum on that interval. At one fixed dose, the marginal statistic reduces to the Banerjee--Wellner law \(D(0)\).
body.justification: The reduction checks both the spatial factor and the fixed-point normalization against known theory.
body.gap: The fixed-dose reduction is known from Banerjee and Wellner (2001); the growing deterministic interval is the new simultaneous component.
body.consumer: The constant-coefficient clock and fixed-dose reduction are valid diagnostics, not a proof of the growing-domain law.

obligation.what_is_open: The constant-coefficient clock and fixed-location identities are proved, but the proposition's invocation of the three growing-domain inference theorems cannot be certified while those theorems remain open.
obligation.obstruction: Constant-coefficient substitution determines the canonical interval length and fixed-origin functional but supplies no excursion, observed-law transfer, or feasible calibration theorem.
obligation.attempted: The spatial integral was evaluated exactly, the canonical coordinate was shown affine, and translation of a single constraint location to the origin was checked.
obligation.partial_result:
Suppose \(f(a)=f_0\), \(\theta'(a)=r_0\), and \(\kappa(a)=\kappa_0\) on \(J\).  Substitution into \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal V(P)=|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},
 \qquad
 T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
The canonical coordinate has constant derivative
\[
 n^{1/3}\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}
\]
and therefore maps \(J\) affinely to an interval of exactly the displayed length.  At a single fixed dose, translation places the constraint at the origin, and \(\texttt{def:canonical-field}\) gives the marginal functional \(D(0)\).  These are exact reductions.  They do not supply the growing-domain excursion theorem, the observed-law coupling, or feasible calibration invoked by the remainder of the proposition.
